To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a data structure, based on priority search trees and red-black trees, which permits us to perform the insert, delete and find-most-specific operations on dynamic router tables comprised of (log n) pairs of tuples in O(log n).
we developed the first O(logn) dynamic data structure for router-tables with conflict-free ranges.
we develop a data structure for dynamic routing tables with O(log n) time for each of the operations of inserting, deleting, and finding the tuple with the most specific matching-range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a dynamic router-table data structure with ranges that is suitable for high-speed routers.
the following questions: (1) How to design a data structure for a dynamic router table that supports insertions, deletions, and lookups in O(log n)?
the following problems: (1) How can we efficiently implement a router table that supports ranges in a way that allows us to perform each operation (i.e. insert, delete, find) in O(log n)?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work is a very nice and useful contribution to the area of routing and packet switching.
the proposed data structure for dynamic range-based routing tables is the most efficient one known today.
the data structures presented in this paper are the most efficient data structures for dynamic router tables, with ranges, to date.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data structure we develop is the first one to achieve O(log n) performance for all the basic operations in dynamic router tables with a conflict free set of tuples.
we have developed a novel data structure for dynamic conflict-free range-router tables with logarithmic time complexity for each of the operations.
we develop a data structure for dynamic routing table that is O(log n) in all operations, and is the first such data structure for dynamic range-based routing tables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with a suitable data structure, the performance of dynamic router-tables with ranges can be improved significantly.
the priority-search tree can be a useful tool for the design of data structures in networking.
, in the context of dynamic router tables, the use of priority search trees can provide a significant speedup over the use of other data structures.
